edits.match: The airways themselves are nourished not by the pulmonary circulation but by small bronchial arteries that arise from the thoracic aorta (one of them, on the right, often from a branch of the arch), run along the bronchi into the lungs and supply their walls down to the bronchioles.
edits.replacement: The airways themselves are nourished not by the pulmonary circulation but by small bronchial arteries: the left arise directly from the thoracic aorta and the single right bronchial artery usually from the third or fourth posterior intercostal artery; they run along the bronchi into the lungs and supply their walls down to the bronchioles.
edits.reason: WRONG: StatPearls (Anatomy, Thorax, Bronchial NBK537353) gives the right bronchial artery's usual origin as the third or fourth intercostal artery (or a superior intercostal / left superior bronchial artery), not 'often from a branch of the arch'.

notes: GENERAL KNOWLEDGE (correct): origin at cricoid, oesophagus behind, thyroid isthmus and strap muscles in front, aortic arch over the left main bronchus, carina at sternal angle, 16-20 C-shaped rings with trachealis, right main bronchus wider/shorter/more vertical (foreign bodies), 3 right and 2 left lobar bronchi (lingula), 10 right / 8-10 left segments with named RUL and RML segments, cartilage plates in bronchi diminishing to none in bronchioles, bronchial veins to azygos and pulmonary veins, vagal constriction/secretion and sympathetic relaxation, cough reflex at carina, conducting zone. 'Nervous pathway that inhaled drugs for asthma exploit' is loose (beta-agonists act on receptors, anticholinergics on the vagal pathway) but not wrong. Clinical text consistent with MedlinePlus and the cited Sheffield Children's guideline (not retrieved). Structures valid (atlas includes 'Bronchial branch of arch of aorta' as a variant); references https on approved hosts.
